_comment: EXT-17 M6 - the committed twenty-run campaign. CR-EX-7, CR-PAR-2 and CR-DOC-2.
The same axis M5 decided (OQ-4): the closing speed of the Red raid in
Atacama Air Defense, applied as one declared scalar to named entities before start. The
scenario authors every raider at 55 m/s on a fixed heading, about 8.6 km out from a
defended cluster, and a 1200-frame run is 60 s - so the speed decides how far the raid
gets inside the window, and whether the defences engage.
TWENTY VALUES, not seven. [B]'s acceptance criterion 1 asks for a campaign of at least
twenty runs executing unattended, and M5's seven-value sweep was a sweep rather than a
campaign. The values are spaced to put five points below the first threshold, five
across it, and the rest above - so the flip CR-PAR-2 asks for is resolved rather than
merely present. The README reports what the twenty runs measured.
THE RANGE STOPS AT 380 ON PURPOSE. The platform honours an injected speed exactly up to
400 m/s and clamps above it, walking the entity down at 20 m/s^2 - so a value above 400
is not the value that flies, and a sweep crossing it would plot a result against a number
that stopped being true partway through the run. Measured at M5 over seven values, and
recorded as R13: the ceiling belongs to a scenario's entity profiles and NOT to the
campaign runner, so the tool does not enforce it and staying inside it is this file's job.
The gate runs at 55 - the scenario's own authored speed, and one of the values swept. It
establishes determinism FOR THAT VALUE and not for the sweep. Six pairs at one value were
compared while deciding OQ-4: 293 576 samples, zero differing.
Judge this campaign with --conditions examples/atacama-raid.conditions.json.
